brief: JPMorgan's flows-and-liquidity note assesses whether tech-sector bond issuance is pressuring yields. The 2026 increase in tech net issuance, about $260bn (US rising from $140bn to $335bn, Europe near $60bn), is modest against $4.9tr of global bond supply, adding only 10-15bp (5-10bp once policy-rate expectations are controlled for) to Global Agg yields. Corporates are a growing but still minority share of the US duration impulse, and a shrinking share in Europe. Separately, September's sharp deceleration in equity fund flows to near zero, rare outside April 2024, is read as a contrarian signal likely to reverse, based on the April 2024 precedent plus weak retail call-option buying and underperforming retail-favorite stocks. CTA momentum signals for Bund, UST, JGB, gilt and OAT-vs-Bund duration reached extreme negative readings, as low as -1.6, amid the recent sharp rise in yields, before moderating. Equity momentum stayed non-extreme by contrast. The gold/bitcoin debasement trade retreated on rising real yields and the Senate's failure to advance the Clarity Act. Gold ETF outflows fully reversed while bitcoin recovered only about half, and JPMorgan reads bitcoin's relatively elevated IBIT short interest versus GLD as room for bitcoin to outperform gold if hedging demand eases.

cards.claim: JPMorgan estimates the 2026 increase in net bond issuance by tech companies of about $260bn would add roughly 10-15bp of upward pressure to Global Agg bond index yields.
cards.anchor: $260bn increase in net bond issuance by tech companies is manageable and would put perhaps 10-15bp of upward pressure on Global Agg bond index yields

cards.claim: When JPMorgan's regression accounts for changes in 6-month OIS rates, the estimated impact of the $260bn supply/demand deterioration on Global Agg yields falls to about 5-10bp.
cards.anchor: this reduces the impact of a $260bn deterioration in the supply/demand balance to around 5-10bp

cards.claim: JPMorgan forecasts US tech sector net bond issuance across high grade and high yield will rise from around $140bn in 2025 to around $335bn in 2026.
cards.anchor: US tech sector net bond issuance in 2025 was around $140bn in 2025 for HG and HY

cards.claim: JPMorgan forecasts US high grade corporate net bond supply will rise from around $615bn in 2025 to nearly $1tr in 2026.
cards.anchor: a notable increase in HG corporate net supply from around $615bn in 2025 to our forecast of nearly $1tr of net supply in 2026

cards.claim: In the US Agg index, the corporate share of the combined corporate and Treasury duration impulse rose from under 10% in 2025 to around 40% in 2026.
cards.anchor: the corporate index accounted for less than 10% in 2025 and around 40% in 2026

cards.claim: In the EuroAgg index, the corporate share of the combined duration impulse fell from around 40% in 2025 to around 20% in 2026 to-date.
cards.anchor: the corporate index accounted for around 40% of the combined duration impulse in 2025, but this proportion has decreased to around 20% in 2026 to-date

cards.claim: Global equity fund flows saw a sharp deceleration in September 2026 following five consecutive strong months.

cards.claim: JPMorgan's bias is that, similar to April 2024, the current weakness in equity fund flows is likely to prove short lived.

cards.claim: The April 2024 weakness in equity fund flows proved short lived and acted as a contrarian signal as the equity fund impulse re-emerged strongly from May 2024 onwards.
cards.anchor: The weakness in equity fund flows from that rate-driven episode of April 2024 proved a contrarian signal as it was short lived
